sections.h2: How do I reach the Tyrrell County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is at 403 Main Street in Columbia, NC 27925, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 449. The listed phone is (252) 796-2901 and the fax line is (252) 796-0148.

Office hours on the register's own site are 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, with holidays excluded. Plan any visit so that it falls inside those hours. If you are mailing a deed, use the post office box and call first so the office can tell you what else it needs.

Tyrrell County is the least populated of the four counties in a Census comparison used here, with 3,537 residents in mid-2025 across 390.78 square miles of land. That works out to 8.3 people per square mile.

The register's page describes the office as the place where the owner of an interest in property can give public notice of that ownership. The record then protects other interested people against unknown transactions and secret liens.

Documents filed there include old land grants, deeds, deeds of trust, maps, leases, agreements and powers of attorney. The same office issues birth, death and marriage certificates and marriage licenses.

The office also offers a Fraud Alert Notification Service. Anyone who signs up with an email address is automatically alerted if a possibly fraudulent recording appears. Owners of vacant land or of property they do not live at may find the alert useful, since they are not at the parcel to notice anything.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Tyrrell County deed?
sections.html:
The seller. North Carolina law makes the transferor responsible for paying the deed excise tax to the register of deeds of the county where the land is before the instrument is recorded.

The rate printed in G.S. 105-228.30 is $1.00 for each $500.00, or fractional part of $500.00, of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed. The statute splits the proceeds between the county's general fund and the State, with the county able to retain 2% of the State's half.

Do not guess the dollar figure. Ask the closing attorney or title company for the line on your settlement statement, and ask the Columbia office if you are handling a deed on your own. If your land lies in two counties, the county with the greater value receives the tax.

sections.h2: What other costs come with recording in Tyrrell County?
sections.html:
Recording charges are statewide, so Tyrrell County charges what the General Statutes set. Everything below comes straight from the statute pages, and you should confirm any special items with the Columbia office before you send a package.

Statutory charges that can apply to a Tyrrell County recording
ItemFee as printedSource
General instrument, first 15 pages$26.00G.S. 161-10
Each added page$4.00G.S. 161-10
Certified copy$5.00 first page plus $2.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Cancellation of a deed of trustNo feeG.S. 161-10
Excise tax$1.00 per $500.00 or fractionG.S. 105-228.30

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive, and they are collected before filing.

sections.h2: What is the housing market like in Tyrrell County?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts reports a median value of owner-occupied housing units of $164,500 for 2020 to 2024, with 77.8% of homes owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $644, and median household income is $41,685.

The county had 2,052 housing units in July 2025 and issued 18 building permits in 2025. There are 1,547 households, averaging 1.94 people each, and 23.3% of residents are 65 or older. The mean commute is 34.2 minutes, the longest of the four counties in the Census comparison.

  • Population was 4,407 in the 2010 Census and 3,245 in 2020.
  • The July 2025 estimate of 3,537 is 9.0% above the April 2020 estimate base.
  • Persons in poverty stand at 19.5%.

In a county of fewer than 3,600 residents, if the property came to you from a relative, ask a title company to review the chain of title before you list it or accept an offer, and keep any estate paperwork together with the deed.

Persons without health insurance under age 65 are 13.8% in the same table, and 83.5% of adults 25 and older hold a high school diploma or higher. The county also shows 71 employer establishments and 543 employees in 2023.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter after I sell a Tyrrell County house?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order and time of registration.

If your deed is not recorded, a creditor with a claim against you, or a second buyer, could end up ahead of the purchaser. The practical answer is to make sure the deed is on its way to Columbia on closing day, whether through your closer or by your own delivery.

  • Ask when the recording will happen and how it will be submitted.
  • Keep proof of delivery if you mail the deed to P.O. Box 449.
  • Request the recording information once the register has filed it.

sections.h2: How are Tyrrell County property taxes paid and handled at a sale?
sections.html:
State law sets taxes as due September 1, payable at face value until January 6, and then subject to 2% interest from January 6 to February 1 plus three-fourths of 1% for each month after, per G.S. 105-360. A lien for property tax attaches to the parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355.

The county's payment page lists several ways to pay: online, by phone, by mail, at the office, in a drop box, or through a bank's online bill pay. It says card payments carry either a $2.50 or a 2.95% service fee, whichever is greater, and e-check payments an added $2.00 fee. Bank bill pay can take up to seven business days to post, so do not leave a tax payoff to the last day.

For the current bill, tax rate and any prepayment discount, ask the Tyrrell County tax office. The register of deeds does not collect property tax.

sections.h2: Can an heir sell a Tyrrell County house without a full estate?
sections.html:
Sometimes. Under G.S. 28A-25-1, a small estate can be settled by affidavit when personal property less liens is not more than $20,000, no petition for a personal representative is pending, and 30 days have passed since death. A sole-heir surviving spouse can go up to $30,000 after reduction for any spousal allowance.

The affidavit goes to the clerk of superior court in the county where the person lived. It lists each tract of real property the person owned. Whether you can then deed the land is a question for an attorney. Ask the clerk of court about the forms, and ask the register what must be recorded to show the heirs' authority to convey.

faqs.q: What are the Tyrrell County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The register lists 9:00 am to 5:00 pm, excluding holidays. The address is 403 Main Street, Columbia, NC 27925, and the phone is (252) 796-2901.

faqs.q: Is there a fraud alert for Tyrrell County property records?
faqs.a: Yes. The register offers a Fraud Alert Notification Service that emails you if a possibly fraudulent recording is made. Sign up through the register's website.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a deed in Tyrrell County?
faqs.a: The seller pays the excise tax to the register before recording. It is $1.00 for each $500.00 or fractional part of the value under G.S. 105-228.30.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a general instrument in Tyrrell County?
faqs.a: It is $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each additional page, set by G.S. 161-10. Ask the office about any extra charges for your document.

faqs.q: Does the Tyrrell County register collect property taxes?
faqs.a: No. The tax office takes property tax payments, and the county's payment page lists the ways to pay. Ask that office for your bill before closing.
